articles.title: X Money will be the only payout option for U.S. creators
articles.summary: X announced that starting immediately, U.S. creator payouts from Original Content Rewards and Subscriptions must go through X Money, with no alternative payment option offered domestically. X says this lets creators access funds instantly rather than waiting for payout thresholds, but it also requires phone number verification and an active X Premium subscription to qualify for an X Money account. Non-U.S. creators will keep using Stripe for payments. X Money launched in beta in November 2025 and expanded after X partnered with Cross River Bank, which now powers X Money accounts and its Visa debit card, addressing regulatory issues that previously blocked some states' approval due to X's Middle East-linked ownership. The platform remains U.S.-only for now. articles.li_summary: X now requires U.S. creators in its Original Content Rewards and Subscriptions programs to receive payouts exclusively through X Money, dropping alternative methods and mandating phone verification plus X Premium subscription.

articles.title: TikTok signs multi-year NFL deal
articles.summary: TikTok has struck a new multi-year partnership with the NFL that deepens the league's presence on the app. The deal introduces NFL game day hubs built on TikTok's GamePlan sports partnership tool, giving fans a dedicated space to discover trending content, complete fan tasks for exclusive perks, and engage around live game moments. TikTok will also expand year-round storytelling from the league and individual teams, including more game highlights and archival footage. Advertisers gain new opportunities too, with NFL-related trends becoming available through TikTok's Pulse Premiere ad offering. TikTok cited data showing posts tagged #NFL grew more than 32% over the past year, reflecting football's strong presence on the platform. The company also pointed to research showing 59% of TikTok users find watching sports content in-app more entertaining than watching actual games, suggesting the deal reflects broader shifts in how fans consume and engage with live sports content across social platforms.
articles.li_summary: TikTok signed a new multi-year deal with the NFL adding game day hubs via its GamePlan sports tool, more highlights and archival content, and new Pulse Premiere ad opportunities for brands.

articles.title: YouTube adds mobile phone controls for CTV
articles.summary: YouTube rolled out an update letting users control their Connected TV viewing experience directly from their phones, eliminating reliance on standard remotes for tasks like typing comments, reading descriptions, or subscribing to channels. The phone and TV no longer need to share the same Wi-Fi network or be manually paired to sync activity. articles.li_summary: YouTube now lets viewers use their phone as a controller for CTV, syncing comments, likes, subscriptions and search without sharing Wi-Fi, as daily YouTube TV viewing exceeds one billion hours.

articles.title: Pinterest promotes its role in teen wellbeing
articles.summary: Pinterest published a report Tuesday framing itself as a wellbeing-conscious alternative to other social platforms, emphasizing how teens use the app purposefully rather than getting stuck scrolling. The company said 77% of active teen users proactively use its search bar, and teens adjust feed and settings controls at nearly double the rate of other age groups. Teens over-index in art-related searches by 1.26 times, favoring topics like drawing references, anime styles, sketch tutorials and bedroom décor. Pinterest is expanding its distraction-free school-hours nudge feature, launched April 2025, to more than 30 countries; it has already reached 4.5 million teens in the US, Canada, France, UK, Germany and Brazil.
